summary.text: Ashley Hinson is the Republican nominee and the U.S. Representative for Iowa's 2nd Congressional District, first elected in 2020. A former KCRG-TV anchor and reporter in Cedar Rapids, she served in the Iowa House from 2017 before running for Congress. She is running for the open seat of retiring Sen. Joni Ernst (R) and has Ernst's endorsement.

paragraphs.text: Hinson was born in Des Moines, Iowa, in 1983, and lives in Marion, Iowa; her House website calls her an Iowa native.
She earned a bachelor's degree in broadcast journalism from the University of Southern California.

She then worked as a news anchor, reporter and producer at KCRG-TV in Cedar Rapids for more than a decade, and her House website says she was a two-time Midwest regional Emmy award winner and an RTDNA Health Reporting Fellow.
Ballotpedia lists her service with organizations including the Cedar Rapids Metro Economic Alliance, March of Dimes and Junior Achievement of Eastern Iowa.

Hinson was first elected to the Iowa House of Representatives from District 67 in Linn County in 2016, winning the open seat with 62.5% of the vote, and was re-elected in 2018, serving from 2017 to 2020.
Her 2020 campaign website, quoted by Ballotpedia, says she served as House Transportation Chair.
In 2020 she won the Republican primary for Iowa's 1st Congressional District and then defeated incumbent Rep. Abby Finkenauer in the general election, 51.2% to 48.6%.
After redistricting she ran in the 2nd District in 2022 and won, and she was re-elected in 2024.

In Congress Hinson serves on the House Appropriations Committee and the Select Committee on the Strategic Competition Between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party, and Ballotpedia lists her on the Ethics Committee in the 2025-2026 Congress.
Ernst endorsed her Senate campaign on January 10, 2026.
Hinson and her husband, Matt, are raising two sons in Marion, and she plays violin at Antioch Christian Church, according to her House website.
